terms.comment: Of throwing something down or away as unwanted; humī abjicere, to dump on the ground or the floor. Tipping a load out is effundō (pour out).

phrases.latin: et summīs spoliat coriīs contemptaque passim spargit humī atque abjicit
phrases.english: and he strips off the outer skins and scatters the unwanted bits about on the floor and throws them away

phrases.latin: trāditās sibi tībiās, cum ad ōs adhibuisset īnflāssetque, pudēfactus ōris dēfōrmitāte abjēcit īnfrēgitque
phrases.english: when he had been handed the pipes and had put them to his lips and blown, he was so ashamed of how they spoiled his face that he threw them down and broke them

phrases.latin: prō sē quisque, quod cēperat, adferēbat, ante pedēs Pȳthiī piscēs abjiciēbantur
phrases.english: each man brought what he had caught, and the fish were dumped at Pythius’ feet

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-vergilius, loci-gellius, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
